findings.summary: The cosine/dot/L2 relationship for unit vectors is shown as a bare formula chain that fails to say what it means.
findings.evidence: L2^2 = 2 - 2*cos | monotone | Same ranking | all three
findings.fix: Add one plain line: 'On unit vectors, higher cosine = higher dot = lower L2, so all three give the same ranking.'

findings.summary: The 'Which Metric?' section mixes advice with a conclusion, and its 'So: normalise, then use dot for speed' bullet holds two ideas.
findings.evidence: So: normalise, then use dot for speed
findings.fix: Split into 'Normalise vectors' and 'Then use dot product: same ranking as cosine, cheaper to compute'.

findings.summary: Code is shown before the idea behind it is stated, and the Matryoshka bullet holds two ideas.
findings.evidence: Matryoshka models: truncate 3072 to 256, small loss / Re-normalise after truncating / python v = v[:256]
findings.fix: Split the Matryoshka bullet into 'Matryoshka models can be truncated (e.g. 3072 to 256)' and 'Truncation costs a small loss in quality'. Keep the 're-normalise' line directly above the code.

findings.summary: The quantisation table has no rationale and a stray rescoring line, so it doesn't say what is traded away.
findings.evidence: float16 | 1/2 ... binary | 1/32 / Usually rescore top hits on full vectors
findings.fix: Add a 'Cost' column (e.g. float16: negligible loss, binary: largest recall loss) and explain that rescoring on full vectors recovers recall.

findings.summary: Recall is used on the Flat and HNSW pages before recall@k is defined on the next page.
findings.evidence: Page 4: "Exact, 100% recall; fine up to ~100k vectors" and "Fast and high recall"; recall@k is first defined on Page 5: "recall@k = share of the true top-k (from flat search) the index returns"
findings.fix: On page 4, add a one-line gloss at first use, e.g. "recall = share of the true nearest neighbours the index actually returns (measured on page 5)".

findings.summary: The IVF code block is shown before the idea is stated, and the bullet about training holds more than one idea.
findings.evidence: k-means splits vectors into nlist cells; needs a training step
findings.fix: Split into 'k-means splits vectors into nlist cells (clusters)' and 'Needs a training step before adding vectors'. State the idea above the code.

findings.summary: The 'nprobe=1' callout is a stray fragment with no lead-in, and 'Uses less memory than HNSW' is an unqualified comparison.
findings.evidence: nprobe=1 / Fast, but misses neighbours sitting near a cell border. Raise nprobe for recall.
findings.fix: Label it 'Trade-off: nprobe' and add a row for nprobe to a knob table (nprobe | cells probed | more recall, more latency), matching the HNSW knob table.

findings.summary: The post-filter vs pre-filter table rows are inconsistent, so a skimmer could misread which 'Risk' goes with which approach.
findings.evidence: Count | Fewer than k, or zero | Correct / Risk | Selective filter empties results | Slow search, fragmented graph
findings.fix: Merge the 'Count' and 'Risk' rows into one 'Problem' row for each column, and keep 'Fix' as a separate row.

findings.summary: The 'Common Mistakes' list gives only the mistake, with no fix, so the learner has to look elsewhere for the correction.
findings.evidence: No recall measurement / Filtering after a small top-k / Re-embedding with a new model without rebuilding
findings.fix: Use a two-column Mistake | Fix table, e.g. 'Filtering after a small top-k | Overfetch or pre-filter'.

findings.summary: The unit-vector line is garbled and cannot be read as written.
findings.evidence: Unit vectors: cosine dot==, all three rank identically
findings.fix: Write 'Unit vectors: cosine == dot, and all three metrics rank identically'.

findings.summary: The cheat sheet's metric table drops the 'magnitude' behaviour that page 2 teaches, so the two pages differ in what they say about each metric.
findings.fix: Keep the same columns as page 2, or add a 'Magnitude' column (ignored / rewarded / sensitive).
